title: POS orders
description: Orders completed at the Point of Sale till.

help.title: About POS orders
help.overview: A POS order is a sale rung up on a till, or the refund of one. This page is the record of those sales; rows are created by the till and are not created, edited, or deleted here.

sections.title: The states
items: Draft is a held cart parked on the till.
Paid is a completed sale. Cancelled is a held cart that was discarded, or one cancelled when its session was force-closed.
Refunded marks a sale whose units have all been refunded. Each refund is also its own order, linked back to the sale.

sections.title: What a row keeps
sections.body: The order is written when the till takes payment.
items: Session, till, cashier, and the customer when one was attached.
Lines with product, variant, quantity, unit price, discount, tax share, and how much of each line has been refunded so far.
Payments per method, the change given, and the fiscal result (fiscal codes and e-invoice status) when the till fiscalizes.
A link to the mirrored product order that keeps the sale in the order books and revenue.

sections.title: Refunds and reprints
sections.body: Money moves on the till; this page is for finding the sale.
items: Refund a paid sale from the till, in full or by line quantity. A refund cannot exceed what is left on each line.
Reprint, from the row menu, produces the receipt again.
Product orders made by the till cannot be refunded or returned from the Product orders page; that keeps the drawer and the stock in step.
